With XBLOCK=128 fixed, 7840 blocks launch across 132 SMs producing 3 full waves + a partial wave of 1504 blocks, wasting up to 25% of runtime. applicable_when: The kernel copies a contiguous (7840,128) tensor into a strided output (10,128,28,28) with strides (376320,1,13440,480). The current 1D tiling (XBLOCK=128) maps each CTA to exactly one row of 128 elements, but the output store address is x0 + 480*x1 with stride-480 in the row dimension. Consecutive threads in a warp write to addresses 480 floats apart (1920 bytes), causing maximally non-coalesced stores and L1TEX scatter latency. All three prior XBLOCK-enlargement attempts failed correctness because the mask is tl.full([XBLOCK], True) with no bounds check, causing OOB writes when XBLOCK > 128. The fix is to restructure as a 2D kernel: XBLOCK tiles the channel dimension (size 128, output stride=1 -> perfectly coalesced), YBLOCK tiles the row dimension (size 7840). This makes each warp's 32 threads write to consecutive channel addresses (stride-1), achieving full coalescing. Explicit bounds masks on both dimensions prevent OOB.
